scenes.heading: Simplifying Expressions
scenes.subheading: Grade 8 Mathematics · Factorisation and equations, part 2
scenes.narration: Welcome to part two of our series on factorisation and equations. In this lesson we simplify expressions, and algebraic fractions.

scenes.heading: Example 1: Expand and simplify
scenes.narration: Simplify three times, x plus two, minus two times, x minus four. Expand: three x plus six. Then negative two times x is negative two x, and negative two times negative four is plus eight. Now collect like terms: three x minus two x is x, and six plus eight is fourteen. The answer is x plus fourteen.

scenes.heading: Example 2: Divide by a single term
scenes.narration: Simplify twelve x squared plus eight x, all over four x. Divide every term on top by four x. Twelve x squared divided by four x is three x. Eight x divided by four x is two. So the answer is three x plus two.

scenes.heading: Example 3: Three terms on top
scenes.narration: Simplify fifteen a cubed, minus ten a squared, plus five a, all over five a. Divide each term by five a. Fifteen a cubed divided by five a is three a squared. Negative ten a squared divided by five a is negative two a. And five a divided by five a is one. The answer is three a squared, minus two a, plus one.

scenes.heading: Example 4: Factorise, then cancel
scenes.narration: Simplify six x plus nine, over three. Factorise the top: three times, two x plus three. Now the three on top and the three at the bottom are common factors, so they cancel. The answer is two x plus three.

scenes.heading: A common mistake
bullets: Only cancel factors, never single terms
$\frac{x + 6}{6}$ is not $x$: you cannot cancel the 6s
scenes.narration: Here is a very common mistake. You may only cancel factors, never single terms of a sum. In x plus six, over six, the six on top is a term, not a factor of the whole top. So the answer is not x. If you split it, you get x over six, plus one.

scenes.heading: Example 5: Multiply fractions
scenes.narration: Simplify two x over three, times nine over four x. Multiply the tops: two x times nine is eighteen x. Multiply the bottoms: three times four x is twelve x. Eighteen x over twelve x: the x's cancel, and eighteen over twelve simplifies to three over two.

scenes.heading: Tips
bullets: Divide every term on top by the bottom
Factorise first, then cancel common factors
Never cancel single terms of a sum
scenes.narration: To sum up: when you divide by a single term, divide every term on top. When you can, factorise first, then cancel common factors. And never cancel single terms of a sum.

questions.text: Explain why $\frac{x + 4}{4}$ does not simplify to $x$.
answer: Only common factors cancel. The 4 is a term of $x + 4$, not a factor of it.
